answer: One way to slow sybil attacks is to require each agent to lock a refundable bond before trading. The bond sits in escrow and returns only after a clean record over many trades. An attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand bonds, which ties up real capital and makes the attack expensive. A pearl kept in a vault is small on its own and costly in bulk, and bonds work the same way. A shared registry, an atlas of verified agents, lists which bonds are active and which were slashed. Honest agents build history even in a tundra of low activity and keep their bond intact.
